structured_output.analysis: The budget is 84617/26880, about 3.148 bits per weight, and iso_3.15 uses 3.1480 avg bits (E514ab09c524e). So the budget is already full and any method upgrade has to be paid for with a downgrade of the same size. The layers where the loss concentrates are all MLP projections at int3 or int2. Moving one of them down to int2 costs a lot: for example, 27.up_proj measures 0.00572 at gptq_int3 against 0.0269 at gptq_int2 (Ef04d8aa7bded, Ec2994e80f2d5). I don't know which layers are currently at int4 or what they measure, so I can't price a downgrade to pay for an upgrade. For this round I'm only changing GPTQ options, since act_order and damp don't change the stored bits.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Bit-neutral option change. iso_3.15 measured KL=0.4361 at 3.148 avg bits (E514ab09c524e), and the top loss layers are GPTQ int3/int2, e.g. 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065). Setting act_order=true makes GPTQ quantize the columns with the most activation energy first. 27.up_proj has activation kurtosis 1090 (E24beed188b6a), so it may benefit.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Same bit count as iso_3.15 (KL=0.4361, E514ab09c524e). This adds act_order=true and lowers damp from 0.01 to damp=0.005 so GPTQ follows the measured Hessian more closely on the int3 MLP layers that carry the most loss, e.g. 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 at 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5) and 1.up_proj at 0.00611 (E0564bc6ad1eb).
